title: Inference similarity geometry for learned semantic state retrieval
question: Does cosine similarity at inference materially improve target-state retrieval compared with raw dot-product inference on the same trained encoder?
hypothesis: H_eval_geometry: the apparent retrieval improvement seen under cosine evaluation is caused by inference-time normalization rather than a change in training objective.

arms.name: raw_dot_eval
arms.intervention: same trained encoder scored with raw dot product

arms.name: cosine_eval
arms.intervention: same trained encoder scored with L2-normalized cosine similarity

endpoints.name: target_top1_recall
endpoints.role: primary — correct opaque persistent state selected

endpoints.name: target_rank_mean
endpoints.role: secondary — mean rank of correct target state

decision_rule.condition: cosine_eval recall >= raw_dot_eval recall + 0.10 and cosine_eval recall >= 0.50
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that inference-time cosine geometry materially improves the current retriever
decision_rule.does_not_license: general cosine superiority or a learned selective retriever

decision_rule.condition: cosine_eval recall is within 0.05 absolute of raw_dot_eval recall
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that inference metric geometry does not materially change retrieval on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: that metric geometry is irrelevant elsewhere

decision_rule.licenses: evidence that cosine inference is harmful in this configuration
decision_rule.does_not_license: that cosine inference is generally harmful

decision_rule.licenses: partial evidence that inference metric geometry affects retrieval

held_constant: H=64 task anchor and A1 H-invariant query/state stream
dual linear input width=10 and latent width=16
one deterministic positive view per update
the trained encoder is identical across scoring arms
no evaluation address or gold target enters training
prior C5 and learned-state results remain frozen
